junction.name: West Marginal Way South & South Holden Street, Seattle

claims.text: West Marginal Way South & South Holden Street had 26 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $1.8 million a year.
25% of crashes here were recorded as “rear ended” crashes, against 13% at the city's worst crash locations.
14% of crashes here had “speeding” recorded as a contributing factor, against 4% at the city's worst crash locations.
14% of crashes here were recorded as “from opposite direction - one left turn - one straight” crashes, against 6% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 0.8 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $267,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 0.6 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $199,000 a year; check on site: the pavement's friction is low now (wet-road crashes alone do not show it).
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 2nd Avenue South, South Holden Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
The state transportation department (route designation only; confirm ownership) is responsible for West Marginal Way South (signed route in OpenStreetMap; owner not confirmed).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) and the state transportation department (route designation only; confirm ownership) is ready to draft from these facts.
